fixed.q: Under the IBC, interior wall finish is set on wood furring over a fire-resistance-rated or noncombustible wall. If the space behind the finish is not filled with inorganic or Class A material, fireblocking is required at what maximum interval in any direction?
fixed.why: IBC 803 requires furred spaces behind finish on rated or noncombustible elements to be filled with inorganic or Class A material or fireblocked (per Section 718) at no more than 8 ft in any direction.

fixed.fact: OSHA Table D-3 minimum illumination: 5 foot-candles for 'general construction area lighting'; 3 foot-candles for 'general construction areas, concrete placement, excavation and waste areas, accessways, active storage areas, loading platforms, refueling and field maintenance areas'; 5 for indoor warehouses, corridors and exitways and for tunnels and general underground work; 10 for construction plants and shops; 30 for first aid stations, infirmaries and offices.
fixed.note: Both the 5 fc and 3 fc rows mention general construction areas. Exam questions worded 'general construction area lighting' expect 5; items about construction areas listed with concrete placement or excavation expect 3.

facts.reason: Merged two rules: (a)(1) per-shift inspection does not name a competent person; (a)(6) daily sling inspection by a competent person

fixed.fact: Rigging equipment for material handling must be inspected before use on each shift and as needed during use, and defective rigging must be removed from service; slings and their fastenings and attachments must also be inspected each day before use by a competent person designated by the employer.

facts.reason: Only jigsaws with blade shanks 1/4 in or narrower may have a positive on-off control; wider-shank jigsaws need momentary contact

fixed.fact: Hand-held tools such as drills, fastener drivers, grinders and disc sanders with wheels or discs over 2 in, belt sanders, reciprocating and saber saws, and jigsaws with blade shanks wider than 1/4 in need a momentary-contact on-off control, which may have a lock-on that releases with a single motion of the same finger; platen sanders, grinders and disc sanders 2 in or smaller, routers, planers and jigsaws with blade shanks 1/4 in or narrower may have only a positive on-off control.

1926.350(a)(2) says cradle, slingboard or pallet; and cylinders 'shall' be moved by tilting and rolling

fixed.fact: Compressed gas cylinders must be moved by tilting and rolling them on their bottom edges and must not be intentionally dropped or struck; valve protection caps may not be used to lift cylinders, and cylinders being hoisted must be secured on a cradle, slingboard or pallet, never lifted by magnets or choker slings.

IRC trigger is the footing bottom slope; IBC 1809.3 trigger is the ground surface slope; fact applied the IRC wording to both

fixed.fact: Footings must be stepped where the top elevation changes or where a slope steeper than 1 vertical in 10 horizontal (10%) occurs: under the IRC, where the bottom of the footing would slope more than 10%; under the IBC, where the ground surface slopes more than 10%.

facts.reason: Overstated; steel sheet piles are sometimes designed to carry vertical load (e.g., bridge abutments)

fixed.fact: Sheet piles are interlocking sections driven to form a wall that resists lateral (horizontal) earth and water pressure, as in cofferdams and excavation support; they are generally not used as the primary support for vertical building loads.

facts.reason: For fire-retardant-treated wood the rule applies only to exterior or wet/damp use, and preservative-treated wood has exceptions (1/2 in or larger steel bolts, mechanically galvanized fasteners for some uses)

fixed.fact: Fasteners, nuts and washers in contact with preservative-treated wood, and those in fire-retardant-treated wood used outdoors or in wet or damp locations, must be hot-dipped zinc-coated galvanized steel, stainless steel, silicon bronze or copper. Limited exceptions apply, such as plain steel bolts 1/2 in diameter or larger, and FRT wood used indoors follows the manufacturer's recommendations.
